Why aren't cookies stored encrypted in firefox?

Even credentials aren't encrypted until and unless you tell Firefox to do so. It's a trade off between usability and security.

In regards to cookies specifically, there is no facility to encrypt them in Firefox itself. Websites can (and often do) encrypt cookie data before sending them to the client, but some don't. There is nothing to be done short of using disk-level encryption software for your profile.

Why aren't cookies stored encrypted in firefox?

Why would they be encrypted? They are just cookies, and you may want to use them with other programs.

What you don't want is other users reading them, and that can be accomplished by setting the file permissions for the cookie jar to 600.

The source code to Firefox is publicly available, you can send Mozilla a patch to fix that in the browser if you want.
If you are so concerned, wipe your cookies on browser exit.

For those that don't know how: you go to Preferences -> Privacy -> Keep until I close Firefox. This will clear your cookies every time you close Firefox. If you want some sites to keep logged on even after you close you can add individual sites using the "Exceptions" button on the same page.

I highly recommend this auto-cleaning. About exceptions though: you may be tempted to add Facebook and Google as an exception to avoid having to login again every time you open Firefox but try to remember that these are the 2 companies that are most likely to track your activities online so I'd advise against exceptiotning them.
